messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert  inc-2026-0315-09: kv-cache metadata growth spike detected in paged-blockmgr cluster 'eu-west-2'. eviction-rate up 18x, p99 latency for generation routes up ~600ms. auto-mitigation not triggered (threshold mismatch).

emma_oncall: seeing the same in dashboards, traces show continuous-batching windows ballooning to >250ms per batch. batch size jump from 8->40 for some customers.

raj: any idea which config changed? rollout history?

sophia: quick check: config.json for continuous_batching_window was rolled from 20ms to 200ms in canary at 1765429000 (automated rollout). looks correlated.

mike: that matches — that rollout was supposed to be backfilled later but a config flag mismatch caused global apply.

emma_oncall: ok urgent plan: 1) revert continuous_batching_window to 20ms (hotfix) 2) temporarily increase blockmgr memory throttle to reduce eviction churn 3) disable prefix prefetch for high-eviction tenant(s) 4) notify CS.

raj: I can do the config revert. prepping a curl to control plane:

```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood.internal/api/v1/configs/continuous_batching -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"window_ms":20}'
```

emma_oncall: run that with --dry-run first, then apply.

raj: dry-run shows diffs, ok applying now.

(infra-bot): Deploy started: config-continuous-batching revert by raj at 1765432120.

raj: applied, control plane acked, starting gradual rollout to eu-west-2.

sophia: I'm changing blockmgr eviction threshold on the fleet to 0.6 -> 0.75 to avoid aggressive evictions while we stabilize. I'll patch via k8s.

mike: patch command?

sophia: `kubectl -n inference set env ds/blockmgr EVICTION_THRESHOLD=0.75 --all` then rolling restart on the ds.

sophia: applied at 1765432140. infra-bot shows rolling restart initiated.

emma_oncall: cs_alyssa can you ping the top affected customers and say we're investigating a performance regression tied to a batching rollout and we've applied mitigation steps? mention potential RPS drop/latency impact.

cs_alyssa: on it. short note sent to two enterprise contacts (ACME, DataStoreInc). letting them know we're doing a config revert and will follow up with timelines.

mike: monitoring: eviction-rate falling from 18x -> 4x, p99 latency trending down from +600ms to +220ms. good sign.

sophia: there's also a spike in block metadata object count in the DB. looks like some stale metadata wasn't trimmed due to the prefetch change earlier. I'll run a safe GC job to reconcile metadata entries for expired blocks.

emma_oncall: careful with GC, schedule low-priority window and throttle. Provide a dry-run first.

sophia: running dry-run now: `python ops/metadata_gc.py --dry-run --tenant-filter=eu-*`

sophia: dry-run estimate ~120k stale rows, would free ~3.2GB metadata. plan to run GC in 5min with rate-limit 500/s.

raj: can we also temporarily reduce continuous batching global cap so batch sizes can't exceed 12? that's a safer guard.

emma_oncall: good idea. raj, can you apply that after revert finishes?

raj: doing cap change: `curl -X POST https://controlplane... -d '{"max_batch":12}'` applied at 1765432155.

(infra-bot): Config change applied: max_batch set to 12 by raj.

mike: p99 now down to +80ms over baseline. eviction-rate near normal. GC dry-run ok'd, starting GC job with throttle.

sophia: GC started at 1765432165, rate-limited. monitoring DB IOPS and metadata table size.

cs_alyssa: customers replied, ACME appreciates proactive heads-up, they've seen reduced timeouts. keeping them looped.

emma_oncall: nice work. post-mortem items: - better canary guardrails so config rollouts can't global-apply by mistake - add auto-rollback on eviction-rate spike threshold - tune continuous batching to have hard caps per-tenant - add metadata-trim on prefetch change paths - create runbook for live GC with throttles

mike: I'll start an incident ticket inc-2026-0315-09 and attach dashboards + timeline.

emma_oncall: handing off to night oncall @mike at 1765432178. please verify stability over next 2 hours and escalate if eviction-rate >2x baseline or p99 >200ms.

mike: ack, taking over. keeping the thread open. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident inc-2026-0315-09 created, severity=sev2, owner=mike, links: https://incident.redwood/inc-2026-0315-09
